title: The benefits of spring cleaning
paragraphs: You may well have heard of the term ‘spring cleaning’: the act of giving your house a deep clean in the spring months. Even though, for many of us, that ritual of a once-a-year blitz of dirt and grime is dying out, some of us still practise it. However, there could be a good reason the tradition isn’t as popular as it was.

The spring months are associated with new life and warmth – a stark contrast to the cold, gloomy winter that preceded. For protection against the freezing weather outside, people would seal their doors and windows as best they could to keep the heat in. In a time when many houses had fireplaces, open fires would churn out smoke and soot, coating rooms with layers of muck and gunk.

It therefore made sense for people to start cleaning in the spring, when the weather was warmer and windows opened, to freshen up their houses, swabbing the floors and cleaning the walls. However, open fires are no longer commonplace in modern British homes, with people preferring central heating to filthy smoke. And it’s not just the way of heating our homes that has changed. In the past, cleaning was designated to specific times and days, as simple chores like washing clothes took a long time. The rise of gadgets such as the washing machine means that tasks are quicker and more efficient.

However, psychologists such as Dr Jonathan Fader, argue that the mental health benefits of clearing the house of mess means that a spring clean is hugely positive. The perception of your house being cluttered can cause the stress hormone cortisol to rise.

So, while the tradition is still there, and it’s nice to have a big purge of dirt once in a while, it is no longer as necessary – or limited to just the spring. That said, the psychological benefits of having a tidy home means that a once-a-year purge of unnecessary items, rather than dirt, can make you feel much better.

vocabulary.entry: spring cleaning /sprɪŋ ˈkliːnɪŋ/ n. 春季大扫除
vocabulary.example: We do a thorough spring cleaning every March.
vocabulary.translation: 我们每年三月都会进行一次彻底的春季大扫除。

vocabulary.entry: ritual /ˈrɪtʃuəl/ n. 惯例；例行公事
vocabulary.example: The family has a ritual of Sunday dinners together.
vocabulary.translation: 这家人有周日聚餐的惯例。

vocabulary.entry: blitz /blɪts/ n. 集中行动；突击
vocabulary.example: The team launched a blitz to finish the project on time.
vocabulary.translation: 这个团队发起突击行动，想按时完成项目。

vocabulary.entry: grime /ɡraɪm/ n. 灰尘；污垢
vocabulary.example: There was a layer of grime on the kitchen walls.
vocabulary.translation: 厨房的墙上积了一层污垢。

vocabulary.entry: stark contrast /stɑːk ˈkɒntrɑːst/ n. 鲜明对比
vocabulary.example: The quiet village is in stark contrast to the busy city.
vocabulary.translation: 这个宁静的村庄和繁华的城市形成鲜明对比。

vocabulary.entry: precede /prɪˈsiːd/ v. 在……之前发生；先于
vocabulary.example: A period of hard work preceded his success.
vocabulary.translation: 他的成功之前是一段艰苦的努力时光。

vocabulary.entry: seal /siːl/ v. 密封；封死
vocabulary.example: We sealed the windows to keep the cold out.
vocabulary.translation: 我们把窗户封死了，好抵御寒气。

vocabulary.entry: churn out /tʃɜːn aʊt/ v. 大量产生；源源不断地生成
vocabulary.example: The factory churns out hundreds of cars every day.
vocabulary.translation: 这家工厂每天生产数百辆汽车。

vocabulary.entry: soot /sʊt/ n. 煤烟；烟灰
vocabulary.example: Soot covered the walls around the fireplace.
vocabulary.translation: 壁炉周围的墙上沾满了烟灰。

vocabulary.entry: muck /mʌk/ n. 污物；烂泥
vocabulary.example: The children got covered in muck after playing in the garden.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们在花园里玩过后，浑身沾满了污泥。

vocabulary.entry: gunk /ɡʌŋk/ n. 黏稠物；污垢
vocabulary.example: There was some sticky gunk on the kitchen counter.
vocabulary.translation: 厨房台面上有一些黏糊糊的污垢。

vocabulary.entry: freshen up /ˈfreʃn ʌp/ v. 使焕然一新；使清爽
vocabulary.example: A coat of paint will freshen up the old room.
vocabulary.translation: 刷一层油漆就能让这个旧房间焕然一新。

vocabulary.entry: swab /swɒb/ v. 擦拭；擦洗
vocabulary.example: She swabbed the floor with a damp cloth.
vocabulary.translation: 她用湿布擦洗地板。

vocabulary.entry: commonplace /ˈkɒmənpleɪs/ adj. 常见的；普遍的
vocabulary.example: Mobile phones are now commonplace in most countries.
vocabulary.translation: 如今手机在大多数国家都很常见。

vocabulary.entry: central heating /ˈsentrəl ˈhiːtɪŋ/ n. 集中供暖
vocabulary.example: The flat has central heating, so it's warm in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这套公寓有集中供暖，冬天很暖和。

vocabulary.entry: designate /ˈdezɪɡneɪt/ v. 指定；指派
vocabulary.example: The room is designated for staff meetings only.
vocabulary.translation: 这个房间被指定仅用于员工会议。

vocabulary.entry: chore /tʃɔː/ n. 家务；日常琐事
vocabulary.example: Washing the dishes is one of my least favourite chores.
vocabulary.translation: 洗碗是我最不喜欢的家务之一。

vocabulary.entry: gadget /ˈɡædʒɪt/ n. 小器具；小装置
vocabulary.example: This new kitchen gadget makes peeling potatoes easy.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新的厨房小工具让削土豆皮变得很容易。

vocabulary.entry: mental health benefit /ˈmentl helθ ˈbenɪfɪt/ n. 心理健康益处
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise has proven mental health benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动对心理健康有公认的益处。

vocabulary.entry: cluttered /ˈklʌtəd/ adj. 杂乱的；凌乱的
vocabulary.example: Her desk was cluttered with papers and books.
vocabulary.translation: 她的书桌堆满了文件和书籍，乱糟糟的。

vocabulary.entry: stress hormone /stres ˈhɔːməʊn/ n. 压力荷尔蒙
vocabulary.example: Long-term stress can increase levels of stress hormones.
vocabulary.translation: 长期压力会导致压力荷尔蒙水平升高。

vocabulary.entry: cortisol /ˈkɔːtɪsɒl/ n. 皮质醇
vocabulary.example: Cortisol is often called the stress hormone.
vocabulary.translation: 皮质醇常被称为压力荷尔蒙。

vocabulary.entry: purge /pɜːdʒ/ n. 清除；清理
vocabulary.example: We need to do a purge of old clothes from the wardrobe.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要把衣柜里的旧衣服清理掉。

vocabulary.entry: unnecessary item /ʌnˈnesəsəri ˈaɪtəm/ n. 不必要的物品
vocabulary.example: She donated all unnecessary items to charity.
vocabulary.translation: 她把所有不需要的物品都捐赠给了慈善机构。

vocabulary.entry: psychological benefit /ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkl ˈbenɪfɪt/ n. 心理益处
vocabulary.example: Keeping a diary can have great psychological benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 写日记能带来极大的心理益处。

sentences.english: You may well have heard of the term ‘spring cleaning’: the act of giving your house a deep clean in the spring months.
sentences.chinese: 你很可能听过“春季大扫除”这个说法：指在春天对房屋进行一次彻底清扫的行为。

sentences.english: Even though, for many of us, that ritual of a once-a-year blitz of dirt and grime is dying out, some of us still practise it.
sentences.chinese: 尽管对我们很多人来说，这种一年一度集中清理灰尘污垢的惯例已经渐渐被淡忘，但仍有人坚持这么做。

sentences.english: However, there could be a good reason the tradition isn’t as popular as it was.
sentences.chinese: 不过，这个传统之所以不像过去那么流行，或许是有充分原因的。

sentences.english: The spring months are associated with new life and warmth – a stark contrast to the cold, gloomy winter that preceded.
sentences.chinese: 春天总是和新生与温暖联系在一起——这与之前寒冷阴郁的冬天形成鲜明对比。

sentences.english: For protection against the freezing weather outside, people would seal their doors and windows as best they could to keep the heat in.
sentences.chinese: 为了抵御室外的严寒，人们会尽可能把门窗封严实，好留住室内的热气。

sentences.english: In a time when many houses had fireplaces, open fires would churn out smoke and soot, coating rooms with layers of muck and gunk.
sentences.chinese: 在过去，许多家庭都有壁炉，明火燃烧会产生大量烟尘，让房间里落满一层层的污垢。

sentences.english: It therefore made sense for people to start cleaning in the spring, when the weather was warmer and windows opened, to freshen up their houses, swabbing the floors and cleaning the walls.
sentences.chinese: 因此，到了春天，天气转暖，窗户可以打开，人们便会着手打扫房屋，擦洗地板、清洁墙壁，让屋子焕然一新，这样做是很合理的。

sentences.english: However, open fires are no longer commonplace in modern British homes, with people preferring central heating to filthy smoke.
sentences.chinese: 但如今，明火壁炉在英国家庭已经不常见了，相比污浊的烟尘，人们更青睐集中供暖。

sentences.english: And it’s not just the way of heating our homes that has changed.
sentences.chinese: 而且改变的不只是供暖方式。

sentences.english: In the past, cleaning was designated to specific times and days, as simple chores like washing clothes took a long time.
sentences.chinese: 过去，打扫卫生被安排在特定的时间和日期，因为就连洗衣服这种简单的家务，都要耗费很长时间。

sentences.english: The rise of gadgets such as the washing machine means that tasks are quicker and more efficient.
sentences.chinese: 而洗衣机这类小电器的普及，让家务劳动变得更省时更高效。

sentences.english: However, psychologists such as Dr Jonathan Fader, argue that the mental health benefits of clearing the house of mess means that a spring clean is hugely positive.
sentences.chinese: 但乔纳森·法德尔博士等心理学家认为，春季大扫除清理屋内杂物对心理健康大有裨益。

sentences.english: The perception of your house being cluttered can cause the stress hormone cortisol to rise.
sentences.chinese: 当你觉得家里乱糟糟的时候，体内的压力荷尔蒙皮质醇水平会升高。

sentences.english: So, while the tradition is still there, and it’s nice to have a big purge of dirt once in a while, it is no longer as necessary – or limited to just the spring.
sentences.chinese: 所以，尽管这个传统依然存在，偶尔进行一次全面的除尘清洁也确实不错，但它已经不再是必需的了——也不再局限于春天。

sentences.english: That said, the psychological benefits of having a tidy home means that a once-a-year purge of unnecessary items, rather than dirt, can make you feel much better.
sentences.chinese: 话虽如此，一个整洁的家能带来心理上的愉悦感，因此每年清理一次不需要的物品，而非灰尘，也能让你心情舒畅不少。
